what: Three pendulums hang freely beside one another. Motor A moves a separate pusher to lift the first pendulum, then withdraws. Follow the first pendulum as it returns and contacts its neighbor. The middle and last pendulums have no motors: their response must come through physical interactions. Compare this contact chain with the supplied model in which the middle pendulum is removed.
try: Load impulse-line.ldr and its matching impulse-line.bw program. Reset the saved model, then press Robot Lab’s toolbar Run. Watch when the pusher touches the first pendulum and when it is clear.
Follow all three bob centers. Which starts moving first? Identify contact and separation instead of using the motor encoder as a measure of the receiver’s motion.
Predict the response with the middle pendulum removed. Run the supplied physical control from its saved pose with the same program and compare the last pendulum’s motion.

Watch what happens after the pusher returns home. Do the pendulums keep exchanging motion indefinitely, or does their motion diminish? Keep the supplied program bounds and reset before repeating after interruption or manual movement.
why: A contact force changes a body’s momentum over the duration of the collision. A moving pendulum can therefore set its neighbor moving even after the pusher has withdrawn. Gravity and the pivots shape the later swing. These contacts are dissipative, so mechanical energy need not remain entirely in visible pendulum motion. Removing the middle pendulum interrupts the intended contact path.
matters: Motion can pass through a chain of unpowered components by brief contacts. Comparing a complete chain with a physically interrupted one helps distinguish that transfer from motion transmitted through the frame. A motor arriving at its target is not evidence that the passive receiver responded.
question: If the pusher returns to the same position in both models, must the last pendulum move the same way? Must one incoming pendulum produce exactly one outgoing pendulum at the same speed?
answer: No. The motor route is the same, but removing the middle pendulum changes the physical path between the launcher and receiver. The receiver’s measured response is the useful comparison. The familiar one-in, one-out result belongs to a carefully aligned, nearly elastic idealization. Distributed LEGO links, pivot reactions, contact losses and the moving frame can produce a different response.
further: Distinguish a contact event from a complete swing. Gravity and the support act throughout the swing, so a finite bob-only observation is not automatically an isolated collision.
Compare the independently observed receiver motion in the complete and interrupted chain. Check the frame at the same time; removing the middle pendulum also changes the load on the support.

Compare Pendulum Array’s freely drifting phases, Echo Bridge’s elastic coupling and Pulse Percussion’s fixed strike bar. This model asks whether intermittent contacts transmit a launch through passive neighbors.

Physical pin friction, material deformation, sound, manufacturing tolerances and impact forces need separate hardware measurements. Do not infer an ideal lossless cradle from the appearance of the model.
formula: Impulse J = ∫F dt = Δp. Over a finite interval, the change in a body’s momentum equals the impulse of all external forces on that body. An internal contact transfers momentum between neighbors, while pivots, gravity and the frame can also contribute.
